evals.name: whole-domain-not-sample
evals.prompt: Break this into stories: requirement A says every save (create, rename, add person, remove person, add expense, edit expense, delete expense) shows the same 'Saving / Saved / Not saved' states and asks for the device's person before the save if none is set. Requirement B says every screen meets the accessibility bar. The UX lists screens for each save. Write the stories with acceptance criteria.
evals.expected_output: The rules in A and B appear as acceptance criteria on every story that adds a save or a screen state, not only on the first story or the one whose journey names the rule.
expectations: Every story that adds a save kind carries the save-states criterion
Every story that adds a save kind carries the ask-for-person criterion
Every story that adds a screen or a screen state carries the accessibility criterion
No story leaves a cross-cutting rule to be inferred from another story

evals.name: plan-from-what-depends-on-it
evals.prompt: Break this into stories: an invoicing module gets a shared test fixture that builds invoices and records what the module emits. Refunds (needs to see credit notes and the ledger entries they produce), disputes (needs to set the invoice's clock and read the dispute's status history) and monthly reports (needs a run over many invoices across two currencies) each build on the fixture. The fixture's first user is the basic invoice story, which only needs totals. After the three, the legacy tax calculator is removed; a comparison test checks the new calculator against it until then. Every code story must pass the type checker. Write the stories with acceptance criteria.
evals.expected_output: The fixture's criteria come from what refunds, disputes and reports need, not only from the first story's totals; the removal story says what happens to the comparison test; the type-checker rule is a criterion on every code story; anything one story promises another is a criterion, not a note.
expectations: The story that builds the fixture has criteria for credit notes and ledger entries, a settable clock and status history, and many invoices in two currencies
The removal story names the comparison test and says whether it is deleted or replaced
Every code story carries the type-checker criterion, including ones that can run in parallel
No promise between stories is left only in a description or note
